newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: C&W unfazed by BT, MCI merger.
newsitem.headline: C&W unfazed by BT, MCI merger.

text.p: The chief executive of Cable and Wireless said on Sunday it remained to be seen how well a merger between competitor British Telecommunications Plc and U.S. firm MCI Communications Corp would work.

BT unveiled the largest merger in British corporate history, linking up with the number two U.S. long distance phone company, MCI Communications Corp. The deal has yet to be agreed by regulatory authorities on either sides of the Atlantic.
C&W chief executive Richard Brown said big did not always mean best in the sector, where his firm was a leading provider of international telecommunications services.

"We are happy with the course of actions we are on the way with. There are mergers appearing all over...This is one more. How well it works, with all the regulatory debates, remains to be seen," Brown told Reuters in an interview.

"We think we have a great business in Cable and Wireless. We are big enough to be successful and independent. We are global and small enough to be nimble in the market place," said Brown, who was in Singapore to open his company's new office on Monday.
"I think the winners of the future will not be the bigger players but the better players," Brown said, saying he was completely unfazed by the tie-up.

BT said the deal would create a world leading communications power house with an annual revenue of over 25 billion pounds ($41 billion), cash flow of about 7.5 billion pounds and 43 million business and residential customers in 70 countries.

Cable and Wireless provides mobile communications in 30 countries and operates the world's largest, most advanced cableship fleet. An attempt by BT to merge with British rival Cable and Wireless failed six months ago. ($1=.6096 Pound)
